# Selector reference

Wherever a command takes the id of a card or group, it also takes a selector. A selector must match exactly one node; when it matches several, the command lists them with their ids so you can pick one.

```sh
orion node show 'label:"Extract slider"'
```

| Selector           | Selects                                                                                                                                                                      | Examples                                                                                                |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label:<text>`     | The node whose label is exactly this text. Quote it with " or ' when it has spaces, so the shell keeps it whole.                                                             | `label:"Extract slider"`<br>`label:'Extract slider'`                                                    |
| `ref:<key or ref>` | The node with this ref. A bare key such as `owner/name#12` or `ABC-12` matches as it's stored, ignoring case, and a URL or `source:key` resolves the way `--ref` does first. | `ref:gummy-galaxy/orion#86`<br>`ref:https://github.com/gummy-galaxy/orion/pull/86`<br>`ref:jira:ABC-12` |
| `pr:<number>`      | The card whose pull request has this number, with or without `#`. A value that isn't a number matches as `ref:` does.                                                        | `pr:86`<br>`pr:#86`                                                                                     |

Selectors match the way [`--where`](./query) does, so `ref:` takes the same keys as `ref = "…"`, and its URLs and `source:key` refs follow the [ref forms](./refs).
